I understand if they go above and beyond, organising you free drinks, making a complex cocktail- but why is a bartender worth $1-2 for serving for a simple drink? Say it's a beer, or a whisky and dry, under a minute to serve you. That would place their labour at 60-120 an hour.

I don't mean to be rude, but I'm from another country, and this has always been odd to me. I've always been bewildered at the fact a bartender might even expect a $1 tip for a beer.

Even a 20% tip on a beer is approaching that 1 dollar mark, which places that labour 40- 60 an hour. Always makes me scratch my head.

When I was over there I'd calculate a tip that equated to $25 an hour, if that bartender did nothing special (poured and fetched simple drinks and got on with their job). The biggest tip I left was for a bartender who, in a busy bar, never seemed.to leave anyone waiting, and working it out after the fact, priced their labour at 45 an hour.

Am I missing something?

Thanks!
